sentences.text: Ceratosaurus is known for a prominent ridge-like horn on its snout and a pair of horns positioned above its eyes.
This bipedal dinosaur moved on powerful legs while possessing reduced arms.
The skull of the largest known specimen is estimated to measure 79 centimeters in length.
The skeleton found in the Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry represents one of the largest-known specimens of this genus.
One significant skeleton was purchased by a private museum and has never been scientifically described.
A life-sized model of the animal appeared in the 1914 film Brute Force, possibly the first live-action dinosaur movie.
The largest known species, C. dentisulcatus, was informally estimated by Madsen to be around 8.8 meters long.
The genus Ceratosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884.
The type species was described based on a nearly complete skeleton found in Garden Park, Colorado, within the Morrison Formation.
The holotype specimen was discovered and excavated by farmer Marshall Parker Felch in 1883 and 1884.
A significant skeleton was discovered in the early 1960s by James Madsen and his team in the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah.
Donald Henderson suggested in 1998 that Ceratosaurus used its long teeth as fangs for quick, slashing bites with concentrated force due to its narrow skull.
Snively and Russell suggested in 2007 that Ceratosaurus could make powerful upward and sideways head movements.
Pathological evidence includes a stress fracture in a foot bone and a broken tooth showing signs of further wear after the break.
Ceratosaurus was a rare member of the theropod fauna, found at an average rate of 7.5 to 1 compared to Allosaurus in sites where both species coexist.
Its crocodile-like tail suggests it may have been a good swimmer.
Ceratosaurus fossils have been found at Garden Park in Colorado alongside Allosaurus remains.
Ceratosaurus gives its name to the clade Ceratosauria, which diverged early from the lineage leading to modern birds.
Madsen and Welles described two new Ceratosaurus species, C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis, in a 2000 monograph.
Ceratosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 155 million years ago, in North America and Europe.
Portuguese Ceratosaurus bones were found in sandstones thought to be late Kimmeridgian in age.
Ceratosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically within the Kimmeridgian and early Tithonian stages, between 156.3 and 146.8 million years ago.
It is debated whether the nasal horn was a weapon or used solely for display, with recent studies suggesting it was for display.
While some paleontologists suggested Ceratosaurus hunted aquatic prey like fish, this hypothesis has been rejected by more recent studies.
Brooks Britt and colleagues suggested in 2000 that C. nasicornis is a juvenile and the other species represent adults of the same species.
Some authors question whether any finds from the Tendaguru Formation belong to Ceratosaurus due to a lack of diagnostic features.
In 1884, Marsh considered the nasal horn of Ceratosaurus a powerful offensive and defensive weapon, a view agreed upon by Gilmore in 1920.
In 2001, Bruce Rothschild and others published an examination of stress fracture evidence in theropod dinosaurs.
They examined a single foot bone of the Ceratosaurus nasicornis holotype and found it had a stress fracture.
If C. ingens is valid, at least one species of Ceratosaurus was as large as Torvosaurus and Epanterias that lived alongside it.
A 2026 study argues that the dentition of Ceratosaurus might have been an adaptation for quickly killing middle-sized prey.
A 2026 study reported evidence that Ceratosaurus skull adaptations suggest similarities in ecological roles with abelisaurs and tyrannosaurs.
